title: Ship Python RAG + agent quickstart template (tools, vector store option, eval hooks)
creator: Monica Patel
description:
Goal
- Deliver a production-minded Python quickstart template that demonstrates: (1) RAG retrieval pipeline, (2) an agent loop that can call tools, (3) safe defaults (timeouts/retries/caps), (4) OpenTelemetry + Redwood conventions, and (5) baseline eval hooks so we can prevent regressions.

Context
- This is the v1 “RAG + Agents” template that will be referenced from docs and used for adoption KPIs. It must be resilient in the face of streaming disconnects and avoid insecure defaults (secrets/PII/logging).

Scope (v1)
1) Template scaffold + local dev
- Repo layout aligned with README standard.
- Local dev server (FastAPI preferred) with streaming response path.
- .env.example with required + optional config.
- Dockerfile + docker-compose for local OTel collector.

2) RAG pipeline (baseline)
- Ingestion: simple file-based loader (e.g., ./data) + chunking defaults.
- Indexing: local vector store option (default) + adapter interface for future hosted vector DB.
- Retrieval: retriever interface w/ structured errors and empty-result handling.

3) Agent loop + tool calling
- Agent orchestrator loop with tool schema validation.
- Guardrails:
  - max_iterations (default 6)
  - tool output size limits (bytes / tokens)
  - tool timeout + circuit-breaker behavior
  - safe error handling that surfaces actionable messages without leaking secrets
- Provide at least 2 tools:
  - retrieve(query): returns top-k passages w/ citations
  - healthcheck(): simple tool to test tool-call path and error handling

4) Model/provider abstraction + model pinning
- Config exposes model + optional fallback model (per PM-913) without hardcoding provider-specific details.
- Support Redwood API/SDK as first-class; keep code structured so alternative providers are possible later without large rewrites.

5) Observability (minimum viable, required)
- Traces (OTel): span hierarchy aligned with quickstart tracing conventions.
- Metrics: latency breakdown, token counts, retrieval hit rate, tool failure rate.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with redaction defaults; propagate redwood-request-id into logs + spans.

6) Evals + regression hooks (minimum viable)
- Add a small eval harness hook (run_eval.py) and a minimal golden prompt set.
- CI should be able to run evals offline (where possible) and smoke tests against the API in a controlled way.

Non-goals (v1)
- No hosted vector DB integration beyond interface/placeholder adapter.
- No multi-tenant auth patterns beyond API key usage.
- No full UI; API-only template.

Acceptance criteria
- “Time to first success” path works end-to-end:
  1) `cp .env.example .env` + set REDWOOD_API_KEY
  2) `make dev` (or equivalent)
  3) `curl`/script returns a streamed answer with citations
- Tool calling works and is observable:
  - trace shows spans for agent loop + tool calls
  - logs include correlation fields and redact secrets
- Safe defaults shipped:
  - request timeout, retry/backoff, max_tokens, concurrency limit documented + enforced
- Retrieval + empty results behavior:
  - if retrieval returns empty, agent returns a safe “no results” response and logs retrieval_empty=true (no infinite loop)
- Evals:
  - `python scripts/run_eval.py` executes a minimal suite and produces a machine-readable output (json) for CI gating

Implementation checklist
- [x] Create base scaffold + README skeleton (align with DES-377)
- [x] Implement config schema + validation helper usage (blocked on ENG-4187; integrate once landed)
- [x] Implement retriever interface + local vector adapter
- [x] Implement agent loop + tool schema validation + guardrails
- [x] Add resilient networking defaults (timeouts/retries/streaming robustness)
- [x] Add OTel spans/metrics/log redaction + request-id propagation
- [x] Add Dockerfile + docker-compose local collector
- [x] Add eval hook + golden prompts
- [x] Add basic CI checks + smoke tests (streaming/tool path)

Artifacts / links
- Confluence: Template requirements (RAG + Agents): sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/template-requirements-rag-agents.json
- Confluence: Observability hooks standard: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/observability-hooks-standard.json
- GitHub PRs (redwood-quickstarts):
  - PR-101 initial scaffold
  - PR-102 OTel + log redaction
  - PR-103 retry/timeout/circuit breaker defaults
  - PR-104 tool-calling agent loop + guardrails
  - PR-105 retriever abstraction + vector adapters
  - PR-106 eval harness hook + golden prompts
  - PR-107 Dockerfile + local collector compose

Notes
- Telemetry tagging for adoption metrics is optional and must remain opt-in (corporate proxies may reject unknown headers). See follow-up work tracked elsewhere.
comments: 2025-02-05 (Monica Patel): Marking as P0 for internal beta. Please keep scope tight: local vector store default + clean adapter interface only. No hosted vector DB until post-launch. Also make sure we align tool schema validation behavior with Dana’s TS plan so docs don’t diverge.

2025-02-07 (Allison Grant): For tracing, please use the standard span names:
- quickstart.request
- llm.chat (or llm.generate)
- rag.retrieve
- rag.rerank (optional)
- agent.loop (with loop.iteration attribute)
- tool.call (with tool.name)
Avoid high-cardinality attributes (no raw prompts, no full URLs, no user IDs).

2025-02-10 (Christine Wong): Streaming robustness: don’t implement silent infinite reconnect loops. If stream breaks, retry at most once for idempotent operations, then surface an actionable error (include redwood_request_id, error.type). Add a small runbook section in README for common proxy/timeouts issues.

2025-02-12 (Marcus Lin): Security review items for template:
- Ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is never printed in logs.
- Redact Authorization header and any env var values in error dumps.
- Provide guidance for sample docs under ./data (no PII). Add a note to not commit customer documents.
- Pin dependencies and document upgrade process (even if CI pinning lands via separate ticket).

2025-02-18 (Sabrina James): PR-101 up with scaffold + env parsing + README skeleton. Next: retriever interface + agent loop. Blocking question: do we standardize on FastAPI for v1? It’s in most examples; I’ll proceed unless objected.

2025-02-19 (Monica Patel): +1 FastAPI. Keep it minimal (one endpoint for ask + one for health). Put ingestion/indexing behind explicit command so users don’t accidentally index large folders by default.

2025-02-24 (Sabrina James): PR-104 (agent loop) ready for review. Added guardrails: max_iterations=6, tool_output_max_bytes=32_000, tool_timeout_s=8. Tool schema validation currently fails closed (template returns 500 + error.type=tool_schema_invalid). Please sanity check error taxonomy alignment.

2025-02-25 (Priya Shah): Support perspective: please ensure the user-facing error message includes a next step. For tool schema invalid, recommend: “check tool returned JSON matching schema; see docs/troubleshooting#tool-schema”. Also include redwood_request_id in error responses so support can find traces.

2025-03-03 (Sahana Iyer): CI note: streaming tests can be flaky. For smoke tests, prefer deterministic short prompts and enforce hard timeouts. If you need retries at the test level, cap at 2 and log attempts so we can diagnose real regressions vs infra noise.

2025-03-06 (Sabrina James): PR-106 adds scripts/run_eval.py + golden prompts. Output format: JSON lines with fields {case_id, passed, latency_ms, notes}. Not including full model outputs in CI artifacts to reduce accidental prompt/data leaks.

2025-03-10 (Monica Patel): Internal beta readiness check:
- README has Quickstart, Observability verification, Troubleshooting
- Default concurrency set low enough to avoid 429s for free-tier users
- Telemetry tagging remains opt-in and documented
If those are done, we can mark ticket Done once PRs merged and a tag cut.

2025-03-14 (Sabrina James): All PRs merged; template tagged v0.3.0 in redwood-quickstarts. Ran through the happy path on macOS + Linux. Remaining follow-ups filed: better 429 guidance and opt-in telemetry header toggle in CLI.
